articles.title: Trump admin tried to get free work from major law firm for arch and Kennedy Center legal battles
articles.summary: The Trump administration unsuccessfully tried to get a major law firm to do pro bono work supporting projects President Donald Trump has championed, such as...
articles.body:
The Trump administration unsuccessfully tried to get a major law firm to do pro bono work supporting projects President Donald Trump has championed, like his triumphal arch and renaming the Kennedy Center, according to a letter obtained by CNN that the firm sent to three Democratic lawmakers on November 5.

US law firm Kirkland & Ellis said it helped the Trump administration and several federal agencies with pro bono work after cutting a deal with the Trump administration to avoid a White House-prompted freeze out. But the major US law firm declined some matters without facing repercussions.

The firm did nearly $12 million of free legal work following the deal to provide $125 million in free legal services to causes that Trump supported.

"(T)his pro bono commitment was for an indeterminate period and could last beyond President Trump's term," the firm told the Democratic lawmakers in the letter this month.

Democrats have been pushing for documents to uncover information about the White House's effort last year to enlist several law firms to contribute pro bono work.

The president had issued executive orders targeting law firms — which were blocked by courts as unconstitutional — that reshaped the legal industry in Washington. The free legal work that came from the deals, which the administration cut separately with several firms that wanted to avoid being subject to executive orders, has been largely opaque.

The Democratic lawmakers are still seeking details on the other law firm deals. The pro bono work that law firms did for the Trump administration is likely to continue to be a major focus of congressional investigations in the new Congress.

Kirkland & Ellis told Democratic lawmakers in the letter that it turned down requests to work on the renaming of the Kennedy Center as well as a request to represent a veterans' group that supported the arch.

It also turned down requests to work on projects related to the Census, challenges to the US Postal Service's transmitting of ballots and representing scientists in litigation related to the Trump administration's climate policy.

The seven-page letter from Kirkland & Ellis to Connecticut Sen. Richard Blumenthal, California Sen. Adam Schiff and Maryland Rep. Jamie Raskin gives an unusual amount of detail about how the firm's deal was cut with the White House, why the firm feared the Trump administration's executive orders and the work Kirkland ultimately did for pro bono causes.

"Between February and April 2025, the Administration devoted significant attention to large corporate law firms—including both Kirkland and its competitors—and aggressively threatened actions that would have been extremely disruptive to the firms, their clients, and their employees," Kirkland's attorney Beth Wilkinson wrote, using language that signaled the firm was now willing to criticize the administration. "Kirkland took the Administration's threat seriously and focused on how it could resolve the inquiry to best protect its clients and its people."

Wilkinson described to the lawmakers how law firms worried that their clients with matters before federal government agencies may avoid hiring firms the administration was punishing, because it could create issues for the clients themselves. She also noted that Kirkland and other law firms were being probed by the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission because of Trump's crackdown on diversity initiatives.

The firm did not turn over the records Democrats sought until after the election.

"We have recently received substantial and profoundly troubling information that this corrupt bargain went much further than originally understood," three Democratic lawmakers wrote in letters to nine other major law firms that cut deals with the administration to promise pro bono work. The Senate and House Democrats are still seeking documents from those firms.

Kirkland's pro bono legal work was provided to the Departments of Commerce and Defense, the US Postal Service, the US International Development Finance Corporation and an "investment entity negotiated between the Trump administration and Japan," according to the lawmakers.

This amounted to more than 2,200 hours of free legal work for Commerce, and about 1,000 hours of work for the three other agencies, Kirkland told the Democratic lawmakers.

While the newly disclosed legal work is a tiny chunk of the firm's total pro bono efforts, the tallies are notable because of how they begin to fulfill the pledge the White House coerced from the firm.

Kirkland also has tallied contributing nearly 15,500 hours of legal work, worth more than $18 million, to the causes of veterans, combating antisemitism, other public servants and a "fair justice system," which were identified in the deal with Trump as causes the firm should support.

The firm noted it had previously represented government entities for free during past administrations, without any deals. That included helping the Secret Service sketch out practices for protecting the president and the White House and representing a Minnesota state agency following the police shooting of George Floyd.

The law firm said, however, it didn't keep records of every time someone reached out on behalf of the administration about a possible client matter, and didn't have any other agreement documents beyond what Trump had announced in April.

"The Trump Administration also unsuccessfully tried to involve Kirkland & Ellis in work supporting the President's political vanity projects, such as the renaming of the Kennedy Center or supporting the illegal construction of his triumphal arch in Washington, D.C.—raising serious questions of whether other firms acceded to these demands," the Democratic lawmakers also said.

A spokesperson for Kirkland didn't immediately respond to a request for comment on Thursday morning.

articles.title: PF prende no DF suspeita de integrar esquema de falsos investimentos que movimentou mais de R$ 600 milhões no PI | G1
articles.standfirst: Kayra Cardoso Guimarães é namorada de "Chico Trader", suspeito de chefiar o esquema. O nome de Kayra estava na difusão vermelha da Interpol.
articles.summary: Kayra Cardoso Guimarães é namorada de "Chico Trader", suspeito de chefiar o esquema. O nome de Kayra estava na difusão vermelha da Interpol.
articles.body:
A Polícia Federal prendeu nesta sexta-feira (20), no Distrito Federal, Kayra Cardoso Guimarães, suspeita de fazer parte de um grupo investigado pela Polícia Civil do Piauí por movimentar milhões com golpes envolvendo falsas operações financeiras na bolsa.

Kayra é namorada de Francisco das Chagas Chaves da Silva, conhecido como "Chico Trader ", suspeito de chefiar o esquema que teria movimentado mais de R$ 600 milhões no Piauí.

O nome de Kayra estava na difusão vermelha da Interpol. Ela foi presa na rodoviária de Taguatinga, no Distrito Federal. A prisão contou com o apoio da Polícia Militar do DF.

De acordo com a Polícia Civil do Piauí, este pode ter sido o maior golpe financeiro já registrado no estado.

A investigação aponta que o grupo atraía investidores com promessas de altos lucros com supostos investimentos na Bolsa de Valores.

Depois de um tempo, os suspeitos deixaram de responder às vítimas, o que as levou a procurar a polícia.

A Operação Extrema Confiança investiga um grupo suspeito de atrair investidores com promessas de altos lucros por meio de supostas operações na Bolsa de Valores.

De acordo com a Polícia Civil, Francisco começou a atuar no mercado financeiro em 2017. Após uma parceria malsucedida que deixou investidores com prejuízos superiores a R$ 100 mil, ele passou a atuar sozinho e fundou a Xtreme Trade.

Em 2023, tornou-se o único sócio-administrador da empresa e intensificou a captação de recursos de terceiros.

Segundo o delegado, o investigado aceitava investimentos em dinheiro, transferências bancárias, joias e veículos, o que dificulta calcular o prejuízo total. Entre cerca de 100 vítimas já ouvidas pela polícia, há perdas individuais que variam entre R$ 200 mil e R$ 400 mil.

articles.title: Gilmar Mendes diz não ver problema em abertura de sigilo de relatório sobre ministros, mas que medida não resolve questão | G1
articles.standfirst: Ministro afirmou ainda ser necessário examinar o conteúdo do material. Nesta sexta (20), após pedido de André Mendonça, presidente do STF levantou o sigilo do relatório sobre Mendonça.
articles.summary: Ministro afirmou ainda ser necessário examinar o conteúdo do material. Nesta sexta (20), após pedido de André Mendonça, presidente do STF levantou o sigilo do relatório sobre Mendonça.
articles.body:
O ministro Gilmar Mendes, do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ), afirmou nesta sexta-feira (20) não ver problema na abertura do sigilo do relatório da Polícia Federal sobre outros ministros do Supremo mencionados ou que trocaram mensagens com o ex-banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro.

"É uma discussão que cabe, talvez, a quem está agora com a própria relatoria, no caso o presidente Fachin. Não vejo nenhum problema se houver esse tipo de decisão e também não vejo que isso solucione a questão, é preciso que se examine de fato o conteúdo".

A declaração acontece após o ministro André Mendonça pedir ao presidente da Corte, Edson Fachin, que "dê ampla publicidade" ao relatório da Polícia Federal com menções a Mendonça no caso Master.

Após o pedido, Fachin atendeu à solicitação e retirou o sigilo do relatório sobre Mendonça, que estava em segredo por determinação do presidente do STF. Os relatórios que tratam de outros ministros do STF seguem sob sigilo.

O relatório sobre Mendonça é um dos documentos enviados pela PF à presidência da Corte nesta semana e que estão no centro da crise do Master no Supremo.

Gilmar Mendes defendeu ainda que o caso Master fosse analisado pelo plenário do Supremo e não pela Segunda Turma.

"Eu já disse em outro momento que me sentia bastante incomodado desta matéria estar na turma. E esse juízo cada vez mais se consolida. Me parece que esse tema deveria vir ao plenário do Supremo Tribunal Federal", disse.

"Certamente, as investigações prosseguiram e esse procedimento talvez seja, ou já, é uma consequência desse processo complexo de investigação. Toda hora aparece um nome ou a citação, ou algo, que às vezes tem relevo, às vezes não tem relevo, seja no campo penal, seja em outros campos. Mas é preciso que nós aguardemos a deliberação de quem tem competência para fazer".

Gilmar Mendes em sessão plenária do STF - 21/10/2026 — Foto: Gustavo Moreno/STF

Nesta quarta-feira (18), o diretor-geral da Polícia Federal, A ndrei Rodrigues, entregou ao presidente do STF, ministro Edson Fachin, o relatório citando todos os ministros do tribunal mencionado s ou que trocaram mensagens com o ex-banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro.

Ao menos cinco ministros confirmaram que o material foi disponibilizado pela presidência do STF. Segundo esses relatos, os documentos só trazem citações a eles. Não há informações sobre colegas.

Ao todo, a PF entregou 10 relatórios a Fachin. Desses, seis já foram arquivados. O presidente do STF encaminhou à Procuradoria-Geral da República (PGR) quatro "para exame e avaliação das providências que entender cabíveis" em 15 dias.

Caberá à PGR avaliar se o conteúdo justifica a abertura de uma apuração, se é preciso aprofundar os fatos narrados com novas diligências, se há dados para medidas mais gravosas, como uma denúncia, ou se é o caso de arquivamento.

Além disso, Fachin informou que as informações recebidas serão mantidas, no momento, em sigilo. Mendonça se antecipou e pediu a divulgação do documento que tem menções a ele.

articles.title: Defesa Civil alerta para chuvas fortes no interior de SP no feriadão | G1
articles.standfirst: A Defesa Civil colocou em alerta para chuvas as regiões de Presidente Prudente, Marília e Itapeva, nesta sexta (20). Regiões de Rio Preto e Sorocaba podem ser atingidas por temporais no sábado (21), com atenção maior para o domingo (22) em todo o interior paulista.
articles.summary: Chuvas fortes durante o feriado prologando podem atingir as regiões de Presidente Prudente, Bauru, Itapetininga, São José do Rio Preto e Sorocaba, a partir desta sexta-feira (20).
articles.body:
Mudança de tempo, com possibilidade pancadas fortes de chuva para Presidente Prudente: Defesa Civil coloca em alerta várias regiões do interior de SP — Foto: Beatriz Jarins/g1

Chuvas fortes durante o feriado prologando podem atingir as regiões de Presidente Prudente , Bauru , Itapetininga , São José do Rio Preto e Sorocaba , a partir desta sexta-feira (20), com atenção maior no domingo (22).

Conforme o alerta da Defesa Civil estadual, a previsão indica aumento das instabilidades ao longo do fim de semana, com possibilidade de chuvas intensas e acumulados elevados em todo o estado no domingo (22).

A Defesa Civil colocou em alerta para chuvas, já nesta sexta, as regiões de Presidente Prudente, Marília , Itapeva , entre outras. Na maioria das regiões do estado, a previsão é de atenção.

As pancadas de chuva podem apresentar intensidade moderada a forte, acompanhadas de descargas elétricas e rajadas de vento, conforme a Defesa Civil.

No sábado (21), o alerta abrange as regiões de São José do Rio Preto, Bauru, Sorocaba, Itapeva e Registro.

As demais regiões paulistas permanecerão em atenção, com previsão de continuidade das instabilidades e possibilidade de pancadas de chuva acompanhadas de descargas elétricas e rajadas de vento.

Os agentes alertam que o período que exige maior atenção será domingo (22), quando há previsão de chuva para todo o estado de São Paulo.

De acordo com os modelos meteorológicos, as precipitações poderão apresentar maior intensidade e persistência, aumentando o potencial para acumulados elevados. Os maiores volumes são esperados nas regiões da faixa leste, norte, noroeste e centro paulista .

Diante desse cenário, a Defesa Civil orienta a população a adotar medidas preventivas:

Alagamentos e enxurradas: não atravesse ruas alagadas nem tente passar por trechos com correnteza, a pé ou de veículo. Mantenha distância de rios e córregos.

Raios e descargas elétricas: procure abrigo em edificações fechadas. Evite permanecer em áreas abertas, próximas a árvores isoladas ou estruturas metálicas.

Ventos fortes: recolha objetos soltos em quintais, varandas e sacadas. Durante as rajadas, mantenha distância de árvores, postes, placas e estruturas que possam cair.

Granizo: procure abrigo em locais seguros, longe de janelas, vidros e coberturas frágeis. Sempre que possível, mantenha veículos em locais cobertos.

Deslizamentos: observe sinais como rachaduras no solo ou nas paredes, inclinação de árvores e postes e movimentação de terra. Ao identificar indícios de risco, afaste-se do local e acione a Defesa Civil.

A Defesa Civil do Estado informou que monitora as condições meteorológicas e mantém atualizações dos modelos de previsão, em articulação com os órgãos municipais e instituições responsáveis pela gestão de riscos e desastres.

A população deve acompanhar os alertas e comunicados oficiais e redobrar os cuidados durante os períodos de chuva. A adoção de medidas preventivas é fundamental para evitar acidentes e proteger vidas, reforçaram os agentes.

Para receber alertas gratuitos por SMS, envie o CEP da localidade para o número 40199. Em situações de emergência, acione a Defesa Civil pelo 199 ou o Corpo de Bombeiros pelo 193 .

articles.title: Embaixada brasileira na Ucrânia é atingida por destroços após ataques a Kiev, diz Itamaraty | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo o Ministério das Relações Exteriores, não há feridos; embaixadas de outros três países também foram atingidas. Sem citar a Rússia, Brasil cobrou respeito ao direito internacional.
articles.summary: Segundo o Ministério das Relações Exteriores, não há feridos; embaixadas de outros três países também foram atingidas. Sem citar a Rússia, Brasil cobrou respeito ao direito internacional.
articles.body:
O Ministério das Relações Exteriores (Itamaraty) informou nesta sexta-feira (20) que a embaixada brasileira na Ucrânia foi atingida por destroços após ataques da Rússia a Kiev .

Ainda conforme o Itamaraty, não houve feridos nem danos materiais à representação brasileira na capital da Ucrânia.

Nesta quinta-feira (19), a Rússia lançou mísseis e drones contra diversas áreas de Kiev durante a madrugada , matando seis pessoas e danificando pontes e infraestrutura de transportes, informaram autoridades locais.

Outras regiões do país também foram atingidas, deixando 28 feridos, segundo o primeiro-ministro ucraniano, Sergii Koretskyi.

"O governo brasileiro condena os ataques a Kiev, na Ucrânia, que impactaram, com destroços de artefatos aéreos não tripulados, as Embaixadas de Brasil, África do Sul, Áustria e Países Baixos em 19 de novembro. O governo brasileiro informa que não houve feridos ou danos materiais à Embaixada do Brasil na capital da Ucrânia", informou o Itamaraty.

Sem citar o governo russo, o Brasil cobrou respeito ao direito internacional.

"O Brasil recorda o dever das partes de respeitar o direito internacional humanitário, incluindo a obrigação de tomar todas as precauções possíveis para minimizar o número de vítimas civis e o dano a objetos civis."

Na nota, o Itamaraty também defendeu que as partes envolvidas na guerra cessem as hostilidades, reforçando que as missões diplomáticas são invioláveis de acordo com a Convenção de Viena sobre Relações Diplomáticas, de 1961.

"O governo brasileiro reitera seu apoio aos esforços diplomáticos em prol de uma solução negociada para o conflito e conclama as partes a avançarem no diálogo, com vistas ao estabelecimento de uma paz duradoura", completou o Itamaraty.

Palácio do Itamaraty — Foto: Reprodução/ Agência Brasília

Lula defende acordo entre Rússia e Ucrânia

Ao longo dos últimos anos, o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) defendeu que os presidentes da Rússia, Vladimir Putin, e da Ucrânia, Volodymyr Zelensky, negociem termos de um acordo de paz .

Em agosto deste ano, Lula conversou por telefone com Putin e, segundo o Palácio do Planalto, manifestou "decepção" com o que chamou de "incapacidade" do Conselho de Segurança da ONU, do qual a Rússia faz parte, de encaminhar uma solução para a guerra entre Moscou e Kiev.

"[Lula] sublinhou a importância do diálogo entre as grandes potências em busca da paz. Nesse contexto , o presidente Lula ressaltou os aspectos humanitários dos conflitos, lamentando a perda de vidas humanas, inclusive civis", completou a nota.

Dias depois, numa entrevista a um podcast, Lula disse ter dito ao "amigo" Putin que ele deveria se reunir com os presidentes Xi Jinping (China) e Donald Trump (EUA) para que os três países pudessem discutir uma solução pacífica para conflitos a nível global . Lula relatou ter tido a mesma conversa com os líderes chinês e americano também.

articles.title: Pedro Sampaio gravou clipe de 'Bate Coxa' em Feira de Santana | G1
articles.standfirst: DJ e produtor musical chegou à cidade dois dias antes do show para filmar parceria com DJ Gordinho Bolado, que tem 1,7 milhão de seguidores no Instagram. Artista carioca fez sua estreia na festa nesta sexta-feira (20).
articles.summary: DJ e produtor musical chegou à cidade dois dias antes do show para filmar parceria com DJ Gordinho Bolado, que tem 1,7 milhão de seguidores no Instagram.
articles.body:
Pedro Sampaio arrasta multidão na Micareta de Feira de Santana 2026 — Foto: João Souza/g1

Feira de Santana entrou no roteiro de uma das novidades musicais de Pedro Sampaio. Antes de estrear na Micareta de Feira, o DJ e produtor musical carioca revelou que escolheu o distrito de Humildes, na zona rural do município baiano, para gravar o clipe de "Bate Coxa", parceria com o DJ Gordinho Bolado, que acumula 1,7 milhão de seguidores no Instagram.

O artista contou que chegou à cidade dois dias antes da apresentação justamente para participar da gravação. A novidade foi revelada durante entrevista nos bastidores da festa, quando Pedro falou sobre os próximos lançamentos e os projetos para o verão.

"Vai, inclusive gravei um clipe aqui em Feira de Santana tem uns dois dias atrás, eu cheguei antes para gravar esse clipe", contou.

A passagem antecipada pela cidade também aumentou a expectativa para o encontro com o público feirense. Conhecido por apresentações cheias de energia e por hits que costumam dominar as pistas, Pedro não escondeu a empolgação com a estreia na festa.

"Estou muito, muito feliz com a minha estreia e empolgado para subir nesse trio e fazer um espetáculo para a galera".

O DJ também adiantou que o público pode esperar novidades nos próximos meses. "Estou preparando alguns lançamentos até o final do ano, podem esperar bastante coisa boa", prometeu.

Pela primeira vez, a Micareta de Feira é realizada em novembro, e não em abril. Os shows começaram na quinta-feira (19) e seguem até domingo (22), no Circuito Maneca Ferreira, na Avenida Presidente Dutra.

Pedro Sampaio levou funk à Micareta de Feira 2026 — Foto: João Souza/g1

A programação reúne artistas nacionais, bandas locais e blocos que desfilam ao longo dos quatro dias de festa. Entre as atrações que já passaram pelo circuito estão Claudia Leitte e Timbalada.

A festa ainda terá apresentações de Carlinhos Brown, Pedro Sampaio, Tony Salles, Psirico, Léo Santana, Pablo, entre outros artistas.

articles.title: Cantor se emociona com nascimento do filho após ver parto pelo celular | G1
articles.standfirst: Cantor já era pai de duas meninas. Ele destacou emoção ao falar com o g1 nos bastidores da Micareta de Feira nesta sexta-feira (20).
articles.summary: Cantor já era pai de duas meninas. Ele destacou emoção ao falar com o g1 nos bastidores da Micareta de Feira nesta sexta-feira (20).
articles.body:
Thiago Aquino nos bastidores da Micareta de Feira — Foto: João Souza/g1

O cantor baiano Thiago Aquino se emocionou ao falar sobre o nascimento do terceiro filho, João Asaf, durante entrevista ao g1 antes de se apresentar na Micareta de Feira de Santana , nesta sexta-feira (20). O bebê nasceu no último domingo (15), enquanto o artista estava em São Paulo a trabalho, e surpreendeu os pais ao chegar antes do previsto.

Pai de duas meninas, Laura, de 8 anos, e Maria Lunna, de 3, Thiago contou que o nascimento do menino representa a realização de um desejo antigo. Ao relembrar a notícia, o cantor revelou que chorou ao pensar no momento e destacou a semelhança entre ele e o recém-nascido.

"Ontem eu me emocionei, ontem eu chorei, porque é um sonho há muitos anos, e Deus conseguiu realizar", contou.

A semelhança entre pai e filho também foi motivo de surpresa. Segundo Thiago, a mãe dele enviou uma foto de quando era bebê, e ele decidiu mostrar a imagem à companheira, Thayná. A reação veio em forma de pergunta: ela quis saber se aquela era uma foto de João.

"Ela olhou a foto e fez: 'Que horas é essa foto, que horas de João?'. Era eu, novinho. Então, é a cópia fiel", brincou.

O cantor também falou, com carinho, sobre as filhas e contou que a mais nova já demonstra vontade de acompanhá-lo nos compromissos profissionais. Antes de seguir para a micareta, ele conversou com a pequena Lunna, que perguntou por que não poderia ir junto com o pai à festa. Segundo ele, a pequena já estava no camarote para acompanhar a apresentação.

Thiago Aquino anunciou o nascimento do terceiro filho na quinta-feira (19), por meio das redes sociais. João Asaf nasceu no dia 15 de novembro, com 33 semanas e dois dias de gestação, antes do período inicialmente esperado.

Pela primeira vez, a Micareta de Feira é realizada em novembro, e não em abril. Os shows começaram na quinta-feira (19) e seguem até domingo (22), no Circuito Maneca Ferreira, na Avenida Presidente Dutra.

A programação reúne artistas nacionais , bandas locais e blocos que desfilam ao longo dos quatro dias de festa. Entre as atrações que já passaram pelo circuito estão Claudia Leitte e Timbalada.

A festa ainda terá apresentações de Carlinhos Brown, Pedro Sampaio, Tony Salles, Psirico, Léo Santana, Pablo, entre outros artistas.

articles.title: Bebê de 7 dias engasgada é salva por bombeiros em Teodoro Sampaio | G1
articles.standfirst: Família levou a bebê até a Estação de Bombeiros de Teodoro Sampaio (SP). Policial militar aplicou manobra de desengasgo e equipe encaminhou a criança ao hospital.
articles.summary: Bebê engasgado em Teodoro Sampaio é salvo por bombeiros após família buscar socorro em quartel; recém-nascida recebeu manobra de desengasgo e passa bem.
articles.body:
Bombeira do posto de Teodoro Sampaio (SP) aplicou manobra de desengasgo para salvar bebê de 7 dias: família levou criança para reencontro com salvadora, nesta sexta (20) — Foto: Corpo de Bombeiros/Reprodução

Uma recém-nascida de apenas sete dias de vida foi socorrida por bombeiros após se engasgar durante a alimentação com mamadeira, na tarde da quinta-feira (19), em Teodoro Sampaio (SP).

A família levou a bebê até a Estação de Bombeiros do município , onde uma policial militar aplicou a manobra de desengasgo e conseguiu restabelecer a respiração da criança.

De acordo com o 14º Grupamento de Bombeiros, de Presidente Prudente (SP), a equipe realizou o atendimento assim que a família chegou ao quartel com a recém-nascida nos braços.

A soldado Dyrlene, integrante dos Bombeiros, aplicou imediatamente a manobra de desengasgo, conhecida como técnica de Heimlich (saiba mais abaixo) , seguindo o protocolo operacional da corporação.

Na sequência, os demais integrantes da equipe prestaram assistência à criança e fizeram o transporte até o Hospital Regional de Teodoro Sampaio, com apoio da viatura.

Segundo o grupamento, a bebê foi encaminhada em segurança à unidade hospitalar após o atendimento inicial realizado no quartel. Nesta sexta-feira (20), a família fez o reencontro do bebê com a bombeiro que aplicou a técnica de desengasgo. O caso foi divulgado pelo 14º Grupamento de Bombeiros nas redes sociais.

Basicamente, o engasgo acontece quando a comida ou objetos vão para o lugar errado quando se engole alguma coisa. Com isso, o organismo tenta expulsar esse corpo que não seguiu o caminho certo da deglutição (da boca até o estômago).

Se a comida ou o objeto bloquear a traqueia (um tubo que leva o ar que respiramos para os pulmões), a pessoa pode não conseguir respirar.

Esta situação é considerada uma emergência e, em casos graves, pode resultar em asfixia fatal ou perda de consciência temporária. Por isso, ações rápidas são cruciais para prevenir complicações.

Como e por que fazer a manobra de Heimlich?

Fazer essa manobra é importante porque ela ajuda a desobstruir a traqueia .

A manobra de Heimlich é uma espécie de abraço por trás, pouco acima da barriga, para tentar expulsar o alimento ou corpo estranho.

No caso de adultos, posicione-se por trás da pessoa e enlace a vítima com os braços ao redor do abdome (se for uma criança, ajoelhe-se primeiro), caso ela esteja consciente.

Uma das mãos deve permanecer fechada sobre a chamada “boca do estômago” ou região epigástrica (veja localização abaixo) .

A outra mão comprime a primeira, ao mesmo tempo em que empurra a “boca do estômago” para dentro e para cima, como se quisesse levantar a vítima do chão.

O Ministério da Saúde orienta que devem ser feitos movimentos de compressão para dentro e para cima (como uma letra “J”), até que a vítima elimine o corpo estranho.

Localização da região epigástrica. — Foto: Domínio Público

Dica: se a pessoa estiver falando, tossindo ou chorando, não faça a manobra, porque a vítima ainda consegue respirar.

📽️📽️📽️ VÍDEO: Abaixo, confira reportagem do Fantástico que mostra como fazer a manobra de Heimlich em bebês, crianças e adultos:

Faça até 3 tentativas. Se a pessoa não responder ou não conseguir respirar depois disso, ela pode estar evoluindo para um quadro de parada cardiorrespiratória. Peça ajuda! Precisa acionar o 190 por telefone e tentar uma reanimação cardiopulmonar.

O telefone de emergência para acionar o Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) – válido para todo o Brasil – é o 192.

Primeiro, coloque o bebê de bruços em cima do seu braço ou sobre a perna. Vire a cabeça dele para baixo, segure a boca até ficar meio aberta e faça cinco compressões firmes entre as escápulas (no meio das costas).

Dê batidas vigorosas nas costas para conseguir realmente empurrar esse corpo estranho.

Com um dedo, abra a boca da criança. Proteja o tórax e vire a criança de barriga para cima em seu braço para observar se ela continua com dificuldades para respirar.

Se ela continua com dificuldades para respirar, faça cinco compressões torácicas. Coloque dois dedos na linha entre os mamilos e empurre contra o tórax da criança por cinco vezes por cinco segundos.

Tente visualizar o corpo estranho e retire-o da boca delicadamente. Se não conseguir, repita as compressões até a chegada a um serviço de emergência.

🚨 O Ministério da Saúde lembra que esses procedimentos são válidos somente se a criança ou o adulto engasgado estiverem conscientes.

Vítimas inconscientes precisam de atendimento hospitalar rapidamente, e os primeiros socorros para asfixia ou engasgo devem ser tomados até que seja possível o atendimento especializado.

articles.title: Flávio Bolsonaro: Moraes vê obstrução e vota por restrições | G1
articles.standfirst: Primeira Turma do STF analisa recurso da defesa do parlamentar contra medidas cautelares impostas por Moraes, como entrega de passaportes e proibição de contato com investigados.
articles.summary: Flávio Bolsonaro é alvo de voto de Alexandre de Moraes no STF para manter restrições após o senador viajar aos EUA em meio a investigações de lavagem de dinheiro.
articles.body:
O ministro Alexandre de Moraes , do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ), afirmou que a fuga do senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) do Brasil demonstra atuação com potencial para obstruir investigações em curso sobre suposta lavagem de dinheiro.

O magistrado votou para manter as medidas cautelares impostas ao parlamentar , como a entrega dos passaportes e a proibição de contato com outros investigados, caso do advogado e amigo de Flávio Willer Tomaz.

🔎Em outubro, o STF abriu um inquérito, sob relatoria de Moraes, para investigar suspeitas de lavagem de dinheiro e vazamento de dados envolvendo o senador Flávio Bolsonaro e o advogado Willer Tomaz.

A Primeira Turma do STF começou a julgar nesta sexta-feira (20) um recurso da defesa de Flávio contra as medidas determinadas por Moraes . Os votos podem ser inseridos no sistema eletrônico do STF até o dia 30 de novembro.

Moraes ressaltou que Flávio descumpriu a ordem judicial para entrega dos passaportes e estava proibido de deixar o país.

“O investigado evadiu-se do território nacional, violando o dever de permanência no país e a obrigação de entregar os documentos de viagem. Os elementos demonstram a efetiva atuação do investigado, com potencial para obstruir as investigações em curso, por meio da fuga do distrito”, escreveu o ministro.

Segundo o ministro, as investigações estão em andamento e as restrições devem ser mantidas porque são necessárias à efetividade do processo .

“[O recurso] não apresentou qualquer argumento apto a desconstituir os fundamentos apontados”, declarou.

Flávio Bolsonaro desembarca nos Estados Unidos após fugir do Brasil — Foto: Eva Marie Uzcategui/Reuters

A Procuradoria-Geral da República disse que as restrições são proporcionais, fundamentadas e adequadas. A PGR afirma que os fatos investigados são graves.

O Ministério Público Federal afirmou que não há dúvida de que Flávio Bolsonaro recebeu a notificação, transgrediu e fugiu, mesmo sem ordem de prisão, agindo com desprezo.

"A insubmissão às ordens provindas do STF reafirma a necessidade de manutenção das providências impostas, cujos pressupostos permanecem inalterados", declarou a PGR.

articles.title: Xanddy revela segredo do sucesso do casamento com Carla Perez | G1
articles.standfirst: Artista destacou a união da família em entrevista ao g1 nos bastidores da Micareta de Feira de Santana. Xanddy está entre as atrações desta sexta-feira (20).
articles.summary: Artista destacou a união da família em entrevista ao g1 nos bastidores da Micareta de Feira de Santana. Xanddy está entre as atrações desta sexta-feira (20).
articles.body:
O cantor Xanddy revelou o segredo para manter um relacionamento duradouro. Casado há 25 anos com a dançarina Carla Perez , o artista revelou os elementos que considera fundamentais para manter a relação saudável.

"A caminhada, num casamento, tem suas dificuldades, mas com respeito, com paciência, com amor e diálogo, tudo dá muito certo. Mas tem que ter paciência, respeito, compreensão, amor… aí dá tudo certo", afirmou.

O comentário foi feito em entrevista ao g1 , nos bastidores da Micareta de Feira de Santana , onde o artista se apresenta na noite desta sexta-feira (20) . Questionado pelo portal, ele destacou a trajetória de união ao lado da amada. No início deste mês, o casal celebrou Bodas de Prata e aproveitou a ocasião para passar uma temporada no México.

"A gente conseguiu, num determinado momento da nossa relação, eu diria que depois de sete anos praticamente de relação, entender tudo isso. Ficou fácil a gente seguir juntos e aqui estamos nós, felizes, comemorando Bodas de Prata, 25 anos de casados. Eu torço para que todo mundo consiga ter relações assim também", incentivou, reforçando a importância da maturidade na família.

Xanddy comanda trio elétrico na Micareta de Feira 2026 — Foto: João Souza/g1

Além de falar sobre a vida pessoal, Xanddy comemorou o reencontro com o público de Feira de Santana. O cantor, que já participou de outras edições da micareta, destacou a importância da cidade para a construção da carreira artística.

"Eu tenho um carinho muito grande e gratidão, porque Feira faz parte da minha história, da minha carreira, de uma forma muito forte. Até por estar aqui mais pertinho de Salvador, no próprio início da minha carreira, quando as coisas estavam acontecendo em Salvador, Feira já estava abraçando [o trabalho]", relembrou.

Neste ano, Xanddy também celebra 30 anos de carreira e pretende levar um repertório especial para a festa. O artista contou que vai resgatar músicas que não costuma apresentar há bastante tempo.

"Estou celebrando 30 anos de carreira, a gente vai plantar essa história. Então, tem muitas músicas que eu não cantava há muitos anos, como 'Nordestino', 'Overdose de Carinho', 'Te Desejo', 'Peneira' e tantas outras. Hoje o povo vai, com certeza, lavar a jega", antecipou.

Pela primeira vez, a Micareta de Feira é realizada em novembro, e não em abril. Os shows começaram na quinta-feira (19) e seguem até domingo (22), no Circuito Maneca Ferreira, na Avenida Presidente Dutra.

A programação reúne artistas nacionais, bandas locais e blocos que desfilam ao longo dos quatro dias de festa. Entre as atrações que já passaram pelo circuito estão Claudia Leitte e Timbalada.

A festa ainda terá apresentações de Carlinhos Brown, Pedro Sampaio, Tony Salles, Psirico, Léo Santana, Pablo, entre outros artistas.

articles.title: ‘We’ve Got Time’: Trump Suggests Iran War Will Continue Into 2027
articles.summary: The President told news outlets that he was not rushing to make any major decisions about renewed fighting until January.
articles.body:
President Donald Trump suggested he is putting off any major decisions on Iran until 2027, amid reports that he's considering renewed major operations in the war that continues despite repeated promises that it'll end soon.

Speaking to Reuters on whether new major strikes are possible—the U.S. has engaged in limited strikes on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz—Trump, who was en route to Washington following his trip to China, said, "Well, I'll talk to you about it after the beginning of the year." He added: "We've got time."

Trump made similar comments in other interviews. "We'll see what happens after January 1st," the U.S. President told Fox News in an interview that aired on Thursday, just before his summit with China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin . He also told Axios in a phone call Thursday that he was "not rushing into any decision" on Iran.

The President initially promised that the war with Iran would only take weeks, but it has dragged on to nearly nine months, though major hostilities have subsided. Trump has previously said that the war would end immediately after the Nov. 3 midterm elections , but the impasse between Iran and the U.S. remained. And in the past weeks, he's alternated between publicly threatening Tehran and holding off on authorizing new strikes at the request of American allies in the Gulf .

Israel has reportedly tried to convince Trump of a new joint strike. The New York Times reported that the U.S. President is considering a new round of extensive military strikes on Iran, after Tel Aviv warned of Tehran's "success in rebuilding its missile and drone arsenals and advancing its chemical and biological weapons programs." Benjamin Netanyahu, the Israeli Prime Minister whose premiership is in limbo , is reportedly pushing for a four- to seven-day airstrike campaign on Iran.

Axios reported, citing unnamed sources , that the White House sought input from the Pentagon and intelligence experts on how Iran would respond to the strike scenarios prepared by the U.S. military. Axios also reported that any U.S. campaign would involve Israel and could include strikes on Iran's nuclear facilities such as Pickaxe Mountain, energy and other infrastructure, and Iranian military and civilian leaders.

The U.S. midterm elections, in which Democrats won control of Congress as the American public largely rebuked Trump and the Republican Party following their handling of the Iran war and the economic fallout it caused, could complicate decisionmaking. Before the Nov. 3 elections, Trump said that Iran was willing to strike a deal, but after the GOP's stunning losses, which Iranian leaders celebrated , the Administration's messaging pivoted to maintaining economic sanctions and the blockade on Iran.

Vice President J.D. Vance has blamed the war for the GOP's election losses, but still appeared to defend the President's foreign policy on Iran . The Vice President earlier said there was no difference between the President and members of his Administration on the war, but as Vance voiced his misgivings, Trump ordered the Vice President to shift his focus away from Iran diplomatic negotiations and toward domestic policies.

Trump has a small window to push through further military action against Iran before the newly elected Democrats take office in January. On Thursday, the GOP-led U.S. Senate rejected a measure aimed at curbing the war .

Trump addresses reported 'dirty bomb' threat

In the interview with Fox News, Trump said he thinks people should not be alarmed by reports of a planned " dirty bomb " attack on Washington, D.C. A dirty bomb combines conventional explosives like dynamite with radioactive material.

"If it does happen, we wipe them out," Trump said.

Trump acknowledged , however, that intelligence indicated Tehran is potentially interested in biological weapons. "Iran is looking at gases, looking at bio, because we've shut them out with the nuclear," he said, referring to the damage that the U.S. has claimed it dealt to Iran's nuclear facilities .

Iran's foreign ministry refuted Trump's recent statements. "The allegations keep changing, but the underlying narrative remains disturbingly familiar," spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei said in a post on X . "Once again, the world is apparently expected to suffer a bout of collective amnesia."

Baqaei then referred to how the U.S. justified its invasion of Iraq in 2003, alleging that the government of the late Saddam Hussein was developing weapons of mass destruction, which subsequent investigations found to be untrue.

"We find ourselves facing ominous new allegations," Baqaei said, "and a narrative that appears to be following the same fraudulent script."

articles.title: Biden memoir draws fire for ‘denial’ as critics flag Gaza, racial-equity omissions
articles.summary: Joe Biden's memoir "Promise Me, America" draws sharp reviews; critics say he stays "stubbornly in denial" about his age, Gaza, and his 2024 reelection bid.
articles.body: Former President Joe Biden’s new memoir has drawn sharp criticism and opened a debate about how Biden’s choices — and his account of them — will shape his legacy. Released Nov. 17, "Promise Me, America" defends Biden’s presidency and his decision to seek re-election in 2024. The memoir drew a sharp verdict from The New Yorker writer Amy Davidson Sorkin, who said Biden remains "stubbornly in denial," while other critics scrutinized the book's account of Gaza and what it left out about racial equity. Sorkin’s criticism centers on Biden’s response to questions about his age and his continued insistence that he could have won. "The true test of a book like this is whether its author will own his losses, too. Biden, for his part, does not," added New York Times nonfiction critic Jennifer Szalai. "He is so preoccupied with burnishing his legacy that he gets awkward and defensive when addressing the two issues many readers will be most curious about: his handling of the war in Gaza, and his decision to run for a second term." "The news of the memoir, in short, is that there is no real news: Biden is as stubbornly in denial as ever, " Sorkin wrote. BIDEN ADDRESSES INFAMOUS 'WE BEAT MEDICARE' DEBATE MOMENT IN NEW MEMOIR The dispute around Biden's recollection of his tenure centers on two consequential decisions — his choice to seek another term and his administration’s policy toward Israel during the Gaza war. In its review of the memoir, the Associated Press reported that Biden says he believed he was the best person to defeat President Donald Trump and that the Democratic primaries gave him no warning he was in trouble. Meanwhile, Sorkin and Szalai argued in their reviews that Biden gives too little weight to concerns about his age and fitness when recounting that period, despite acknowledging that his debate performance was poor. "Biden’s voice gets passive; he portrays himself as the helpless victim of events," Szalai wrote. "He gets similarly defensive when recounting the war in Gaza," she added. BIDEN ACCUSES PELOSI OF WORKING 'FURIOUSLY' BEHIND SCENES TO DERAIL HIS 2024 CAMPAIGN Self-described socialist website Jacobin and other reviewers, including Sorkin and Szalai, criticized Biden's accounting of his relationship with Israel and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, arguing he described it in the book as if it were much more adversarial than in actuality. Szalai wrote that Biden gets "awkward and defensive" when addressing both Gaza and his decision to seek another term, and faulted him for how he described Israeli victims and suffering versus Palestinian victims and suffering. She specifically noted that Biden used names to identify Israeli victims but "no names" for Palestinian victims, while calling his language about Palestinian suffering "passive." "The only consistent position is inconsistency," Israeli journalist and political commentator Amit Segal said of Biden’s account of Israel policy, calling it "devoid of doctrine or strategy. Weigel wrote that the word "equity" does not appear in the memoir once. articles.title: Fired White House press secretary Katie Zacharia under California state bar investigation
articles.summary: Zacharia’s spokesperson called allegations she falsely represented herself as an attorney ‘baseless’
articles.body:
Katie Zacharia, the former White House press secretary hired and fired in the same week , is under investigation by the state bar of California for claiming to be a lawyer despite never passing the bar exam.

Earlier this month, the state bar of California informed Campaign for Accountability, a non-profit watchdog group, that it had assigned an investigator and legal adviser to investigate Zacharia after the organization filed a complaint.

Before her short stint as Donald Trump 's press secretary, Zacharia repeatedly represented herself as a lawyer on cable news programs and had claimed on her LinkedIn profile that she served as the general counsel for a non-profit organization in California.

Trump also identified Zacharia as an "attorney" when announcing her appointment.

While Zacharia received a law degree from Pepperdine University in 2011, she never passed the bar exam in California or any other US state .

"Zacharia may have thought she was just playing a lawyer on TV, but by repeatedly holding herself out as an attorney on news programs, she was pretending to have authority she lacks," Michelle Kuppersmith, the director of the Campaign for Accountability, said in a statement.

"We're pleased the California bar is taking this matter seriously and investigating," Kuppersmith added.

A spokesperson for Zacharia said in a statement to the Guardian: "These are baseless allegations. This complaint is politically motivated and a clear waste of the state bar's time and resources. We are confident it will be dismissed with no finding of wrongdoing."

Zacharia previously defended describing herself as a "lawyer", claiming there was a difference between a "lawyer" and an "attorney", a title reserved for those licensed to practice law. In her email to the Guardian, Zacharia linked to an American Bar Association Journal article distinguishing the two terms.

A spokesperson for the state bar of California said it was aware of media reports about "non-licensee Katie Zacharia" and that investigations were confidential.

"The state bar notes that neither the submission of a complaint nor the conduct of an investigation constitutes a finding that a non-licensee has engaged in unauthorized practice of law in violation of California statutes," the spokesperson said.

The Campaign for Accountability had submitted a complaint to the state bar of California in mid-October.

"In California, calling yourself a lawyer without a license isn't puffery; it's a crime. The state bar should investigate whether Ms Zacharia has misled the public about her credentials and hold her accountable if she has," the non-profit watchdog organization wrote in their complaint.

Zacharia became the shortest-serving White House press secretary when she replaced Karoline Leavitt in mid-October for just five days. From the start, she struggled to fit into the role, stumbling over words during her first press briefing and only taking questions from predominantly conservative media outlets.

articles.title: Trump defends calling Putin a friend but says he ‘can’t speak’ to whether he's a friend to the US
articles.summary: WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump doubled down Friday on his description of Vladimir Putin as a friend but said he “can’t speak” to whether the Russia...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump doubled down Friday on his description of Vladimir Putin as a friend but said he "can't speak" to whether the Russian president is a friend to the U.S.

Trump also insisted during a White House news conference that Putin wants peace with Ukraine , despite Russia's continued aggression after invading more than four years ago. Asked about the most recent attacks — hours after Putin met with Trump in China — Trump suggested that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Putin share equal responsibility for the ongoing conflict.

"He'd love to end the war," the U.S. president said of his Russian counterpart. But "you have two guys that don't know how to end it. We're trying to help them. You have two people that hate each other, Zelenskyy and Putin. They don't know how to end it. They want to end it. They're both stuck in it."

During a wide-ranging news conference, Trump praised both Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping after returning from China, where he participated in bilateral and trilateral meetings with his fellow heads of state.

Trump raised eyebrows on the trip with his warm greeting of Putin and repeated references to him as his "friend." He made no effort in the White House briefing room to walk back the comments. And he noticeably sidestepped a specific question about whether he views Putin as a friend to the United States.

"I can't speak to America," Trump said, without expounding.

He shifted immediately to his "very good" personal relationship with Putin and repeated longstanding grievances over the extended federal probe that concluded that Russian agents sought to influence U.S. voters in the 2016 presidential election on Trump's behalf.

"I consider him to be somebody that I have a very good relationship (with)," Trump said. "It's actually very good."

"I've been dealing with Putin" since "the fake Russia, Russia, Russia hoax," as Trump calls the Department of Justice investigation into the 2016 election. "It was a hoax made up by the Democrats" and "probably helped me win," Trump said.

Trump praises relationship with Putin after major Russian attack on Ukraine

Trump spoke warmly of Putin just hours after Russia carried out a nighttime bombardment of Ukraine, killing at least eight civilians and wounding more than two dozen, Zelenskyy said. Russia fired more than 400 drones and over 110 missiles, 27 of them ballistic and some carrying cluster warheads that scatter dozens of smaller bomblets across a wide area, the Ukrainian president said.

Putin had vowed to retaliate for Ukrainian strikes this week that severely damaged the Kerch bridge linking occupied Crimea with the Russian mainland, which is vital to Moscow's war effort. The Russian attack fit the pattern of heavy responses to eye-catching Ukrainian attacks and added to uncertainty about the prospects for the talks brokered by Washington.

Meanwhile, two Russian missiles and a suspected drone also came down in Poland on Friday in what its prime minister said was likely a provocation timed to coincide with European military exercises in his country for a possible postwar mission in Ukraine. There was no immediate comment from Moscow on the incursion or the drills.

Despite Moscow's latest aggression, Trump said Putin has expressed a desire to see the war between Russia and Ukraine end "by diplomatic means." Trump said "there's a real good chance" that a peace deal can be brokered.

Russia rejects Kushner's claims of progress

U.S. envoy Jared Kushner said on Thursday that he believes Russia is "comfortable" with NATO-like security guarantees for postwar Ukraine. Ukraine has long sought entry into NATO, particularly for its common defense guarantee under the alliance's Article 5, which holds that an attack on one member is considered an attack on all.

"I think we've gotten the Russians comfortable with that concept where any security guarantee for Ukraine would be based on Article 5," Kushner said. "And I think that that comes with at least what the Russians are saying, which is their intention is when this war is over to not have another war in the future."

But Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov said Friday that even a "quasi-membership" of NATO for Ukraine would be unacceptable, Russia's Interfax news agency reported . Ryabkov said: "We discuss security guarantees primarily in terms of ensuring the security of our own country, and that's what we're talking about."

When a reporter noted Russia's pushback to Kushner's statements, Trump brushed it off, saying that Moscow was unlikely to publicly confirm details from ongoing negotiations.

"It is also a public relations war. And we'll say things and they'll say things," Trump said.

Trump said he didn't want to talk about security guarantees for Ukraine "because we got to get a deal first." He added that the U.S. will be involved when there is a deal.

Rubio rejects criticism that Trump embraces autocratic leaders

Trump insisted his relationships with the other world leaders is key to an eventual peace.

"You know, you're very lucky to have somebody that has a relationship with the heads of the most powerful countries," he said.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who stood on stage during Trump's news conference and made brief remarks, echoed the president's sentiments, pushing back against criticisms that Trump was embracing autocratic leaders as trusted allies.

"I want everybody to understand the relationships between heads of state are invaluable," said Rubio, who traveled with Trump to Asia. "It sets the tone for the entire relationship. It sets the tone for our trade negotiators. It sets the tone for our diplomats." __

articles.title: A child support fight exposed a Trump adviser’s $15 million income
articles.summary: Jason Miller was tapped to be Donald Trump’s first White House communications director, but a scandal ended that job in December 2016 before it even began. M...
articles.body:
Jason Miller was tapped to be Donald Trump's first White House communications director, but a scandal ended that job in December 2016 before it even began. Miller stayed loyal, advising Trump's next two campaigns and regularly defending him on cable news shows.

In 2023, Miller's accountant put his total income at about $879,000. Then, Trump was elected president a second time. And Miller proceeded to make more money than he had in the previous seven years combined.

For the 12 months that ended in September 2026, he put his income at about $15 million, nearly all of it revenue from his two firms, according to a sworn financial statement he filed in court. In that time, Miller was a registered foreign agent for the governments of India and Romania and was in talks to join Trump's White House as an unpaid adviser and began appearing there regularly this summer.

Miller's consulting firm continued receiving payments - about $1.3 million from July through September, bank records show.

The details - some of which have not been previously reported and were recently included in the filings of a long-running Miami court case - offer a rare look at how lucrative Trump's return to power has been for one of his most loyal aides. And they show how much money can flow to a presidential adviser without ever appearing in public disclosures.

It took a child support fight - with the campaign aide at the center of his 2016 scandal - to bring that into view.

In a statement to The Washington Post, Miller said, "I take all ethics, lobbying registration, and financial disclosure obligations seriously and have complied with all applicable requirements."

He said he was under no obligation to discuss his financial records or his court case. Miller did not respond to detailed questions about his time in the White House, his work and specific payments, including what they were for. Testimony about Miller's income during the trial this week was first shared on social media by Grant Stern, a Democratic activist and executive editor of Occupy Democrats, who has followed the case for years.

Miller's bank records filed publicly in court show large payments from the government of India, the hedge fund Bridgewater Associates, the media company formerly called Paramount Skydance and a Japanese conglomerate - along with millions of dollars from sources the records do not identify.

His gross income had already begun to climb in 2024, while he worked on Trump's campaign; his accountant put it at about $1.6 million that year. In the 12 months that ended in August 2025, it reached about $4 million. By this fall, Miller's two firms - SHW Partners and a second company, Scipio Strategic, both of which he owns outright, according to his filing - had together brought in about $15 million over a year.

Scipio, which took in $6.7 million of that, does not appear in any public lobbying or foreign-agent filings, so who paid it, and for what, is not publicly disclosed.

Most senior White House officials must publicly disclose their finances. Miller was different. His public lobbying and foreign-agent filings - which, by law, cover only payments received for disclosable activity - account for about $2.4 million of his income over the past two years.

On Nov. 3 - Election Day - Miller wrote in a sworn financial affidavit he filed in the case that he "is currently an unpaid special government employee." Where the form asks for his pay rate, the filing says "unpaid employee." Where the form asked for his employer, he wrote "the White House."

In an unsigned statement Thursday, the White House said: "Jason Miller was never an SGE [special government employee] at the WH. We have enjoyed many different thoughts and opinions throughout this administration and will continue to do so. Our campus remains open to friends old and new, from either side of the political spectrum." The White House did not respond to further questions about what Miller's role was.

When asked about the White House's statement, Miller said, "I never completed the formal onboarding process."

Had Miller become a special government employee, he would have been exempt from federal limits on outside income and employment that apply to most White House staff, according to the Office of Government Ethics. But conflict-of-interest law would have barred him from working on government matters affecting his own financial interests or those of his clients, unless he received a waiver, said Kathleen Clark, a law professor at Washington University in St. Louis who studies government ethics.

She said his lack of official status meant he could operate without committing to follow rules. "What you are describing is someone who has not sworn allegiance to this country, who doesn't even purport to act in the interest in the public and is allowed to go running roughshod around the White House," she said.

Few people have been as close to Trump's political operation and for as long as Miller. He was the chief spokesman for Trump's 2016 campaign, and after the election Trump named him White House communications director. But within days, Miller withdrew amid reports of his extramarital affair with A.J. Delgado, another campaign aide who gave birth to their son in 2017.

He spent the next decade working his way back - as a senior adviser on Trump's 2020 and 2024 campaigns, as chief executive of Gettr, the pro-Trump social media platform, and as a vocal Trump booster. Joining the campaign in 2020, he said he was "humbled by the opportunity for a second chance to serve President Trump."

This summer, Miller started showing up regularly at the White House. Delgado, meanwhile, has sought child support from him in court since 2017; the case had never gone to trial until this month. Ahead of that trial to set regular child support, she subpoenaed his financial records.

The firms' bank statements, filed as an exhibit in the case, identify many payers by name. But for some wire transfers, they show only a date and an amount. In a summary she filed with the court before the trial, Delgado identified the senders of those wires. In Florida family cases, parties must exchange financial records, and Delgado also subpoenaed Miller's bank records; not all of those records were filed with the court. Her monthly totals closely track the income Miller reported under oath.

Most of Miller's income last year came through his lobbying firm, SHW Partners, according to his filings. Its clients have included India, as the country has negotiated for better trade terms, the hedge fund Bridgewater Associates and the public relations firm Teneo, bank records show.

Some clients had business before the Trump administration.

A foreign government, a hedge fund and a media giant

In April 2025, SHW Partners signed a $150,000-per-month contract to provide "strategic counsel, tactical planning, and government relations assistance" for India, according to documents filed with the Justice Department. India paid the firm $900,000 in 2025 and $750,000 in 2026 before Miller stopped working for the country in June, the documents show.

As part of his work for India, Miller met with U.S. administration officials including Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, then-White House chief of staff Susie Wiles and others. In January, Miller traveled with Bessent to Minneapolis for a speech by Bessent to the Economic Club of Minnesota. At the time, India was paying his firm $150,000 a month to lobby, and Miller listed Bessent among the officials he contacted on India's behalf.

Paramount Skydance, through a subsidiary called Viacom, paid Miller's firm SHW $420,000 in March and June, bank records show. At the time, Paramount was seeking the Trump administration's approval to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery. The Justice Department cleared the $111 billion deal on June 12, without major conditions - nine days after the last payment to SHW. When the deal closed in October, the newly formed company rebranded as Skydance.

The trading firm Susquehanna International Group, co-founded by billionaire Republican donor Jeff Yass, paid SHW about $234,000 in 10 payments from April 2024 to February 2025, bank records show. Susquehanna is one of the largest investors in ByteDance, TikTok's Chinese parent company. On his first day back in office in January 2025, Trump paused enforcement of a law that would have banned the app.

Spokespeople for Skydance and Susquehanna declined requests for comment.

Other large payments came by wire, and their senders are identified only in Delgado's summary. She attributed about $1.5 million - most of it in installments of $120,000 - to the Brooklyn Nets. The team is owned by Joseph Tsai, a co-founder of Alibaba, a Chinese tech giant that the Pentagon added in June to its blacklist of companies it says aid China's military. Alibaba has said there was no basis for its inclusion.

The Lawfare Defense Fund, a nonprofit that has raised at least $36 million to help pay legal bills for people it considers unjustly targeted by the legal system, according to the New York Times, paid Miller's firm more than $1.4 million in fees, according to Delgado's summary - including $300,000 in late September. Miller told the Times in June that "any payment that my firm may have received from the Lawfare Defense Fund would have been for communications consulting services." The group has not issued any public press releases.

Miller's other firm, Scipio, which he started in 2025, received most of its money in a handful of large payments, bank records show. After June, when Miller was in talks to join the White House, it stopped receiving deposits entirely; the payments that followed went to SHW.

In December 2025, Scipio received a $3.35 million wire transfer that Delgado identified as coming from Celebrus Investments Limited, an investment holding company registered in Mauritius, an island nation that is a hub for offshore finance.

Miller registered in May to work for Romania's presidential administration for a fee of $300,000 as part of a $3.4 million lobbying contract held by the law firm Eversheds Sutherland, aimed at swaying U.S. energy investments, economic development and U.S.-Romania military cooperation.

Bank records show that Eversheds paid Miller's firms $2.45 million, starting about five months before he registered. The records do not say what the payments were for, and it is not clear whether they were related to the Romania work.

In April this year, Scipio received a $100,000 transfer from a sender Delgado identified as Semafor, a week after the news media company hosted its World Economy 2026 summit in Washington.

In an unnamed statement, a spokesperson for Semafor confirmed the payment to Miller's firm Scipio and said it was for consulting services related to guest bookings at events. It's a practice the company does with consultants from both sides of the aisle, the spokesperson said .

The spokesperson also said that Semafor no longer has a relationship with Miller's firm - it ended shortly after the World Economy event.

Three corporate clients - Divergent Technologies, Mesabi Metallics and OKBL USA Holding - paid SHW about $700,000 in total to lobby for them in 2025 and 2026, federal lobbying filings show, and the bank records match. But OKBL also paid Scipio $500,000, in January and June. Because Scipio is not registered to lobby, that money does not appear in the filings; the records do not say what it was for.

Representatives from India and Romania, as well as Mesabi, Eversheds, the Brooklyn Nets, the Lawfare Defense Fund, Teneo, Celebrus and Divergent did not respond to requests for comment. OKBL declined to comment.

Even before this summer, Miller appeared at events and alongside Cabinet members and other advisers. In September last year, he committed to contribute $300,000 to Trump's White House ballroom project, The Washington Post previously reported, and attended a dinner at the White House a month later for nearly 130 donors to the project.

The Post reported in late June that the White House was in talks to bring Miller on to help with its messaging ahead of the midterm elections. By late July, he was photographed in the Oval Office.

The payments continued. In the first days of July, SHW received $300,000 from Eversheds and $75,000 from Teneo; later that month came $75,000 from Bridgewater. On Aug. 18, a $450,000 deposit arrived with no payer listed. Delgado wrote in her summary that Miller testified in a Nov. 9 deposition that he did not know its source. In late September came two wires, for $300,000 and $120,000, that she attributed to the Lawfare Defense Fund and the Nets.

A Bridgewater spokesperson said that Miller's firm provided "strategic advice to the firm" but "that engagement was proactively paused when the firm learned that Mr. Miller was considering a formal government role."

Miller's registration as an agent of Romania remained active until Aug. 4, and SHW reported lobbying for three corporate clients through July 31.

By the fall, Miller was appearing at key moments alongside the administration's most senior officials. Last month, Miller reportedly interrupted an interview that Katie Zacharia, the new press secretary, was giving the Wall Street Journal in her West Wing office, telling her that Vice President JD Vance wanted to speak with them. She did not return to the interview, and her time as press secretary soon ended, the Journal reported.

In late October, Miller was part of a small group that helped secure a charter jet to fly Flávio Bolsonaro - a Brazilian senator and the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro - from Argentina to Miami after he lost Brazil's presidential runoff election, the Wall Street Journal reported. Brazil's Supreme Court had barred Bolsonaro from leaving the country. Trump has said he can stay in the United States "as long as he likes."

The bank records reviewed by The Post do not show payments from the Bolsonaro family.

Beyond the Florida child support case, Delgado has also sued Miller in New York, accusing him of sexual assault. Miller has denied the allegations.

This week, Miller agreed to pay Delgado $22,000 a month in child support, reaching a settlement in the Florida case after years of fighting that has spilled into public view.

Kevin Crowe and Scott Nover contributed to this report.

articles.title: Trump intel chief warned no funding for Musk’s SpaceX without answers on Ukraine Starshield slowdown
articles.summary: The incoming Democratic chairman of a key congressional committee says lawmakers will withhold funding for systems developed by Elon Musk’s SpaceX if stonewa...
articles.body:
A top Congressional Democrat is warning that lawmakers will withhold government funding for systems developed by Elon Musk's SpaceX if the Trump administration and tech billionaire refuse to disclose who is responsible for ordering the slowdown of Ukraine's military-grade Starlink satellite service, CNN has learned.

In a classified communication sent to Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, Democratic Rep. Jim Himes — who will become chairman of the House Intelligence Committee in January — demanded clarity on what led to the slowdown of Ukraine's Starshield connection speed on multiple occasions in recent months, according to an excerpt of the communication obtained by CNN.

"Simply, our committee cannot authorize funds for the development of government systems that the government will not fully control," Himes wrote to Clayton. "I appreciate your assistance in obtaining transparency in this instance so we can have confidence going forward in authorizing funding for the development of systems using SpaceX as the primary vendor."

The warning comes as a growing number of Democrats have vowed to investigate the limits on Ukraine's Starshield system, which Ukraine relies on for its defenses. After two rounds of days-long speed restrictions, there has been little clarity on who is responsible. Democratic lawmakers in both the House and Senate have said they plan to scrutinize the Trump administration's broader dealings with Russia when the party takes control of Congress in January.

Himes' determination to investigation the slowdown comes as Zelensky has said in recent days that the Starshield system is facing limits once again, while Ukraine is facing massive renewed attacks from Russia even after Trump met with Putin earlier this week.

Himes has also formally requested a meeting with Musk to discuss the slowdown, according to a separate letter sent to the SpaceX CEO obtained by CNN.

"My ask to you is straightforward. Explain the changes that were made to the Starshield service in October 2026, why those changes were made and whether those changes were made unilaterally by SpaceX or were directed by a US government official," Himes wrote to Musk.

"My view, which I have conveyed to senior Administration officials, is that SpaceX's potentially unilateral modification of a US government contract, combined with its lack of responsiveness to congressional oversight, calls into question every contract the US government has with SpaceX, including the development of what you describe as the separate military-grade 'systems owned and controlled by the US government,'" the letter to Musk states.

CNN has reached out to SpaceX for comment.

When Himes becomes chairman of the House Intelligence Committee in January, one of his top priorities will be investigating Musk's control over SpaceX systems like Starshield and, if needed, leverage the power of the purse to extract answers from the company about the slowdown, according to a source familiar with his thinking.

The most obvious tool at Himes' disposal for doing so is known as "ring fencing," which allows the committee to legally restrict funding for certain projects in the annual Intelligence Authorization Act until certain conditions are met.

Himes could also work with congressional appropriators to redirect or block additional funding for SpaceX systems if the company and Trump administration continue to stonewall lawmakers.

According to Himes, the classified message to Clayton and the public letter sent to SpaceX raise two primary concerns: a lack of clarity around who made decisions that impeded Ukraine's defense, and the lack of responsiveness from relevant government entities, as well as SpaceX, to questions from lawmakers to date.

The limitations were in place for several weeks in October. Earlier this month, Zelensky said that renewed limitations were in effect over the occupied territories of Ukraine. Those restrictions have now been in place for more than a week. Denys Sienik, Ukraine's top diplomat in the US, told CNN Friday that they are in touch with the Pentagon but have received no response from SpaceX.

SpaceX maintains billions of dollars in US government contracts for space-based systems, occupying a uniquely critical role in national security as a result. Those contracts are a source of leverage for lawmakers but following through on any threat to restrict funding for SpaceX systems carries the risk of compromising irreplaceable assets the US relies on for its own national defense.

The Trump administration, Musk and SpaceX executives have offered various accounts of who authorized the throttling of Ukraine's Starshield connection speed, a move that led to the disruption of its military internet service and slowed down a critical system for launching missile and drone attacks, as well as defending against Russian strikes.

The initial issues with Starshield were discovered in mid-October after the Trump administration threatened to withhold intelligence to Kyiv over its strikes on Russian refineries and after Trump made a deal to buy Russian diesel and ease sanctions on Moscow. The US president had sparred with President Volodymyr Zelensky and suggested Ukraine should get a new leader.

Reports about that slowdown in the Starlink service led to confusion inside the White House, where many officials were initially unsure what, if any, role the US government had played.

The Senate Foreign Relations Committee is also planning to investigate the Starshield slowdown once Democrats assume the majority in Congress, CNN previously reported. Last week, the outgoing top Democrat and incoming chair of the committee sent a letter to Musk demanding that he and SpaceX preserve documents related to the disruptions.

While Trump advisers were aware of his frustrations with Zelensky before he lashed out publicly, they had not heard the president discuss specific plans to hamper Kyiv's ability to strike Russian diesel refineries, which he has blamed on rising global energy prices.

Trump told officials he wanted to find out where the slowdown originated and would later tell reporters he wasn't personally involved in the decision. Officials inside the administration understood that as a directive to investigate the matter and look into how the system was slowed down.

Privately, SpaceX executives and defense officials have told some inquiring lawmakers that the decision to initiate the slowdown in October originally came from the White House, a source familiar with those discussions told CNN, though Trump has repeatedly denied any direct involvement.

Ultimately, top Trump officials appeared to put responsibility on the privately owned SpaceX and its "terms of service" with Ukraine.

The exact nature of those terms of service as they relate to Ukraine's ability to use Starshield are largely classified, according to a source familiar with the matter.

But there are conditions and caveats for allies like Ukraine to share the capability, meaning Ukraine's use of Starshield is "very dependent upon the US saying yes" with specific contract clauses that allow them to do it, the source added.

The Pentagon's arrangement with SpaceX for Starshield is complicated by the "Elon factor," the source acknowledged, pointing to Musk's unique level of authority at the company allowing him to dictate program changes from the top down.

But Starshield is still a government-managed application, the source added.

"SpaceX flies it on behalf of the of the U.S. government, but the U.S. government is completely in control of how it gets tasked, how it gets used, who gets access to it," they said.

"Starshield is a Pentagon system," one of the sources, a US official, also reiterated, drawing a distinction between SpaceX's role in managing the military-grade satellite system compared to how the company operates its commercially available version, known as Starlink.

Yet a Pentagon official told CNN that Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth had no involvement or foreknowledge of the slowdown – raising further questions about who was ultimately responsible.

"He had no idea it was happening," the official said, referring to Hegseth.

In the immediate aftermath of the slowdown, some Trump officials began pointing the finger at Musk, saying he "went rogue" and acted unilaterally. Trump made no such request to throttle Starshield, one senior US official told CNN at the time.

"Elon did it unilaterally," another US official previously insisted.

Lawmakers on both sides of the aisle have raised concerns about the prospect of Musk using his seemingly unprecedented powers over government-managed systems, like Starshield, to unilaterally enact foreign policy on behalf of the US.

Both Democratic and Republican lawmakers had called for a Pentagon watchdog investigation into the slowdown and whether it, in combination with issues in early missile warnings, put American personnel at risk. But that request was declined by the Pentagon Inspector General who instructed lawmakers to direct their questions to the relevant military service branches.

"There is an outcome where it was actually really bad activity and contravention of a Pentagon contract or maybe (SpaceX) did something they were entitled to do but just did not give anybody any warning," Himes told CNN in an interview this week.

"But we are going to get to the bottom of it. There is a lot at stake here," he added.

In his letter to Musk, Himes stresses that the authorization of US government funding for all SpaceX systems is at risk if the tech billionaire refuses to provide answers.

"It is difficult for me to continue supporting the authorization of funding for these SpaceX-developed, government-owned systems, until I receive satisfactory answers to my questions about the Starshield service in Ukraine," he wrote to Musk.

For more CNN news and newsletters create an account at CNN.com
